- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) and prices are trending upward, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.  
- When sentiment spikes to 1.00, model frequently overreacts; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome by 2–5% over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion bias: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day from forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early sharp decline after a spike, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 1–3% in first 3–5 days post-spike.  
- If sentiment history shows no recent sentiment (all 0.00), model tends to be overly conservative; increase forecast by 0.5–2% to reflect latent market momentum.
